transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-19
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Rivera (Aurelia CTO), Rajesh Singh (Head of Infra), Emily Park (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to align on private networking (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), regions and data residency, egress constraints, and benchmark success criteria/timeline for a 4-week pilot. Action items captured at end.

Topics:
- Networking options: VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, Transit Gateway implications
- Data residency: EU vs US patient data, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM considerations
- Benchmarks: throughput, p99 latency, token cost, failure scenarios
- Timeline: benchmark next week, pilot week after, go/no-go decision criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for hopping on, i'm samir from redwood, and with me is lena, our se. want to kick off with quick intros and high level goals for today's scoping.
[00:18] Maya (Aurelia CTO): yeah thanks samir, i'm maya, ct o at aurelia. our main goal is to run a short pilot for clinical note generation and triage summarization, but must be private networked into our VPCs and strict data residency for EU patients.
[00:32] Rajesh (Aurelia Infra): rajesh here. we manage aws infra, we'll own the networking and security side. curious about latencies across regions and egress cost implications.
[00:44] Emily (Compliance): emily from compliance — SOC2 is table stakes, also need audit logs and key management integration.
[00:52] Lena (Redwood SE): great, thanks. high level i'd like to confirm assumptions: typical payload size ~2-3k tokens per request, expected peak qps ~12, steady at 3-4 qps; for pilot we'll target 50k tokens/day. is that roughly correct?
[01:10] Maya: yes that's accurate, some doctors will send longer notes but average near 2k tokens. timeline wise we want a 2-4 week pilot followed by expansion if numbers look good.
[01:26] Samir: perfect. on networking, we can support two primary private patterns: vpc peering from your VPC into our dedicated networking infra (works cross-account, low-latency within same region) or aws privatelink / interface endpoints where we put an nlb in our svc subnet and you connect via private link endpoints. each has tradeoffs.
[01:44] Rajesh: can you run through tradeoffs briefly? we have strict egress controls so we prefer not to run traffic over public internet.
[01:52] Lena: sure — vpc peering is simple, direct L3 routes, no extra hops but peering is region-local (can't peer across region without transit gateway). private link provides a managed ENI in your account, it's easier for egress control because traffic is to an endpoint, but private link incurs per-hour/GB cost and has some NLB latency overhead. transit gateway can centralize multi-region attachments but adds complexity and cost.
[02:20] Maya: do you support bringing your own private deployment into our VPC? i.e., customer-managed instance inside our subnet or on-prem?
[02:28] Samir: we have Redwood Private options — private control plane with a customer-managed networking model. for on-prem or air-gapped we can discuss an on-prem package, but for this pilot the usual pattern is AWS PrivateLink or peering into a dedicated account/vpc we manage for customers on dedicated capacity.
[02:44] Rajesh: what about cross-region? a portion of our users are EU-based, patient data for EU must remain in EU datacenter. can redwood pin model endpoints to eu-west-1?
[02:56] Lena: yes we can pin regionally. for data residency we can deploy dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 and expose endpoints only in that region. that also avoids egress charges if processing happens inside the EU account. but if you route requests from an EU VPC to a US endpoint you'll incur cross-region egress.
[03:14] Emily: audit logs and key management — we need integration with our KMS keys, H S M, and ability to have access logs for requests for compliance.
[03:24] Samir: we support customer-managed KMS for Redwood Private and Dedicated with envelope encryption. audit logs (request metadata, timestamps, model version) can be exported to your CloudWatch or S3 with restricted access. we will share our SOC2/ISO attestation; lena will attach the security pack after the call.
[03:44] Maya: excellent. benchmarks — what do you want from us to run meaningful tests?
[03:50] Lena: ideally we get a small harness — a container or curl script that simulates traffic with your average token length distribution. test scenarios: steady-state qps, burst to peak qps (12 qps), and a long-seq test (8k token worst-case). metrics: avg latency, p95/p99, tokens/sec, and token cost. we also want failure injection (simulate network drop) to verify graceful fallback.
[04:18] Rajesh: for the pilot we can provide a harness and a subset of anonymized notes — can you run tests in both EU and US regions?
[04:26] Lena: yes, we'll schedule two bench runs: eu-west-1 and us-east-1 dedicated nodes. we recommend using a quantized model variant for cost testing (e.g., 4-bit) and a full-fp16 for latency comparisons.
[04:40] Samir: cost note — private link egress costs and data transfer cross-az/region can move the needle. we'll produce a cost estimate with egress assumptions based on your daily tokens.
[04:52] Emily: encryption in transit — we need mTLS between our services and the endpoint, can you support client certs?
[04:58] Lena: we support TLS with mutual TLS for Redwood Private deployments. for PrivateLink/peering typically TLS from your client to the endpoint is used; we can layer mutual TLS on top for extra assurance.
[05:10] Maya: what about IAM/SAML SSO for users and RBAC for audit?
[05:14] Samir: console access supports SSO (SAML/OIDC) and granular RBAC. for the API keys we can rotate and scope keys to models/routes. audit trails show token-level usage per key.
[05:26] Rajesh: network config — what do you need from our side to set up peering or private link?
[05:30] Lena: for peering: your VPC ID, account ID, CIDR ranges (to avoid overlap), route table entries we can propose, and any NACL rules. for PrivateLink: your subnet IDs for interface endpoints, security group rules, and which AZs to create endpoints in. also proxy requirements if you use outbound proxies.
[05:52] Rajesh: we'll share CIDR ranges and route table owners. egress — we have a strict egress gateway to control traffic to third parties, can we keep traffic internal?
[06:00] Samir: yes if we deploy in-region inside your cloud tenancy (private deployment) traffic can remain internal. with PrivateLink, traffic terminates into an ENI in your acct so it doesn't traverse the public internet. with peering it's also L3 internal. cross-region is the main place egress billing shows up.
[06:16] Maya: success criteria for pilot — what are the go/no-go metrics?
[06:20] Lena: propose: p99 latency under 2.5s for standard prompts, failure rate <0.5%, and cost per 1k tokens below X (we'll compute after we get token volumes). also security checkpoints: KMS integration validated, network connectivity via PrivateLink/peering tested, and audit log delivery working.
[06:42] Emily: compliance also needs a written attestation that EU patient data stays in EU, and a clear data retention policy.
[06:48] Samir: we will provide a data residency addendum and retention options — we support short retention or no retention for sensitive records on Dedicated/Private.
[06:58] Rajesh: timeline — can we run the bench next week and then a 2-week pilot?
[07:04] Samir: yes — bench week of 2028-07-26, pilot start ASAP after a successful run. lena will schedule and own the bench.
[07:12] Lena: i'll prepare a bench plan and a small harness. can you confirm the test accounts and share anonymized sample payloads by friday?
[07:20] Maya: we can get sample payloads redacted and share vpc info by thursday.
[07:26] Samir: great. quick note on failure modes — we can configure fallback to a cheaper model or fail closed depending on your SLA preferences. that helps with graceful degradation if capacity is constrained.
[07:40] Rajesh: do you have any bandwidth or throughput guidance per GPU on dedicated? helps with sizing.
[07:46] Lena: approximate guidance: for a quantized 70B variant on an H100-style instance you might see X tokens/sec (we'll put numbers in the sizing doc) — we'll provide recommended node counts to meet 12 qps with buffer. we also include autoscaling/burst config.
[08:00] Maya: do we need a dedicated contract for the pilot?
[08:04] Samir: pilot can run on hosted/dedicated test nodes. usually we use a temporary dedicated pool for predictable perf; commercial contract can be minimal for the pilot. we'll send legal a statement of work after technical signoff.
[08:16] Emily: are there any third-party sub processors we should be aware of?
[08:20] Samir: we'll share our subprocessor list in the security pack; for Private deployments you can avoid subprocessors by using our on-prem option.
[08:28] Maya: okay sounds good. anything else on routing policies?
[08:32] Lena: one more — we can route by policy (region, latency, or cost). for your use-case we'd recommend region-first for residency, with a fallback to another region only if you allow it.
[08:44] Rajesh: if a fallback occurs will that be logged and alerted?
[08:48] Samir: yes, it can generate alerts and trace logs and we'll surface rollbacks in the console.
[08:56] Maya: recap then next steps?
[09:00] Samir: recap — we will: 1) send private networking design doc + diagram (vpc peering and private link options) — samir; 2) lena will share benchmark plan and security pack; 3) aurelia to share cidrs, anonymized payloads and region residency constraints — rajesh/maya; 4) schedule bench for week of 2028-07-26.
[09:22] Emily: i'll validate compliance items and confirm on data retention options by 2028-07-24.
[09:28] Samir: thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites and attach the docs.
[09:34] Maya: thank you, looking forward to the bench.

End of transcript.
